'''Norman WC Powell''' (born May 25, 1993<ref name="ucla_bio">{{cite news|title=Norman Powell Biography|work=UCLABruins.com|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=207913792|access-date=April 25, 2014|archive-date=April 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160408172545/http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=207913792|url-status=dead}}</ref>) is an American and Jamaican professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Chicago Bulls]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Powell played [[college basketball]] with the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]], where he was an all-conference player in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]]. He was selected in the second round of the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], who subsequently traded his draft rights to the [[Toronto Raptors]]. He won an [[NBA championship]] with Toronto in 2019. In 2026, he was named an [[NBA All-Star]] in his only season with the [[Miami Heat]].

Powell was a two-time all-state high school player in California and led his team to a state championship before joining UCLA.  After entering his senior year in 2014–15 as the Bruins' top returning player, he emerged as a team leader and received first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honors.

==Early years==
Powell was born and raised in [[San Diego]], California,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Siddiqui |first=AJ |date=2025-01-02 |title=Los Angeles Clippers' Norman Powell On His Breakthrough Season And His 'Understand The Grind' Foundation |website=[[Forbes]] |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/djsiddiqi/2025/01/01/los-angeles-clippers-norman-powell-on-his-breakthrough-season-and-his-understand-the-grind-foundation/ |access-date=2025-01-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250102162242/https://www.forbes.com/sites/djsiddiqi/2025/01/01/los-angeles-clippers-norman-powell-on-his-breakthrough-season-and-his-understand-the-grind-foundation/ |archive-date=January 2, 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Panerio |first=Jonas |date=2024-08-13 |title=Norman Powell comes back home for his sixth annual youth basketball camp |url=https://athlonsports.com/nba/la-clippers/all-clippers/news/norman-powell-returns-home-to-host-his-6th-annual-youth-basketball-camp |access-date=2025-01-12 |website=Athlon Sports |language=en}}</ref> to Sharon and Norman Powell Sr.<ref name="ucla_bio" /> He was introduced to basketball by his uncle, Raymond Edwards. Powell decided to attend [[Lincoln High School (San Diego)|Lincoln High School]], which had just been rebuilt and lost many athletes.<ref name="painter_0320104">{{cite news|last=Painter|first=Jill|title=UCLA's Norman Powell a slam dunk in San Diego|date=March 20, 2014|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20140320/uclas-norman-powell-a-slam-dunk-in-san-diego|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140426232323/http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20140320/uclas-norman-powell-a-slam-dunk-in-san-diego|archive-date=April 26, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> He helped rebuild their basketball program,<ref name="painter_0320104" /> leading the team to consecutive [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) San Diego Section 2A championships in 2009 and 2010.  The team also captured the 2010 CIF Division II Boys' State Championship, with Powell scoring 24 [[point (basketball)|points]] in a 74–59 win over [[Saint Francis High School (Mountain View)|Mountain View St. Francis]].  He finished his junior season averaging 19.7 points, 4.9 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 2.7 [[steal (basketball)|steals]], and earned first-team all-state as well as Western League Most Valuable Player (MVP) honors.<ref name="ucla_bio" /><ref name="maffei_01132014">{{cite news|last=Maffei|first=John|title=Lincoln's Powell enjoying ride at UCLA|date=January 13, 2014|newspaper=U-T San Diego|url=http://www.utsandiego.com/news/2014/Jan/13/alumni-report-powell/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140429205523/http://www.utsandiego.com/news/2014/Jan/13/alumni-report-powell/|archive-date=April 29, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

In his senior year, he was again first-team all-state and league MVP, and averaged 20.4 points, 3.8 rebounds, 2.4 steals. Lincoln was 32–2 and won the league title with a 12–0 record. They were ranked No. 3 in California and No. 15 nationally, but were defeated 74–69 by Summit in the state semifinals.<ref name="ucla_bio" /> He finished his high school career winning the San Diego County All Star Game Dunk Contest.<ref>{{cite news|last=Angulo|first=Blair|title=In transition with Norman Powell|date=April 27, 2011|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/5787/in-transition-with-norman-powell|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222110429/http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/5787/in-transition-with-norman-powell|archive-date=December 22, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Powell was listed as the No. 15 shooting guard and the No. 52 player in the nation in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/102170/norman-powell|title=Norman Powell Recruiting Profile|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 29, 2014}}</ref> Powell chose to play [[college basketball]] for [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] over [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]], [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] and [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].<ref name="maffei_01132014" />

==College career==
In his first year at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), he was the only true freshman to play significant minutes in [[2011–12 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2011–12]], when he averaged 17.8 minutes and contributed 4.6 points and 2.2 rebounds in 33 games, joining Tyler Lamb and [[Lazeric Jones]] as the only Bruins to play in every game that season.<ref>{{cite book|title=2013–14 UCLA Bruins Men's Basketball Media Guide|date=October 22, 2013 |page=60|publisher=UCLA Athletics|url=http://issuu.com/uclabruins/docs/full_guide_8ad1830246e372/60?e=1901135/5335034|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402135429/http://issuu.com/uclabruins/docs/full_guide_8ad1830246e372/60?e=1901135/5335034|archive-date=April 2, 2015|url-status=live|access-date=April 20, 2020}}</ref> While he excelled as a driving guard in high school, his role transformed at UCLA, taking less than one-fourth of his shots around the rim and close to half from outside on [[three-point field goal|three-point attempts]],<ref name="wang_03102015">{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=Norman Powell is thankful for his UCLA career, both the good and the bad|date=March 10, 2015|newspaper=Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20150310/norman-powell-is-thankful-for-his-ucla-career-both-the-good-and-the-bad|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320233505/http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20150310/norman-powell-is-thankful-for-his-ucla-career-both-the-good-and-the-bad|archive-date=March 20, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> connecting on 38.5% over the last 18 games.<ref name="ucla_bio" />

[[File:Norman Powell with Steve Alford (2) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Powell as a junior in 2014]]
Powell averaged 6.1 points in 22.1 minutes in [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2012–13]], making nine starts while playing all 35 games.<ref name="ucla_bio" /> He began the season as a starter, but was later moved to the bench. His minutes declined from an average of 28.4 in the first seven games to 19 the following 26 games. After replacing injured starter [[Jordan Adams (basketball, born 1994)|Jordan Adams]], Powell's minutes increased to 37 per game.<ref name="yoon_04022013" /> He considered transferring to San Diego State after the season,<ref name="katje_03222014" /> but decided to stay primarily because UCLA coach [[Ben Howland]] was fired.<ref name="yoon_04022013" /> Powell credited Howland for his development on defense, but he stated that "there were a lot of things going on that weren't fair for me" and "I definitely wanted to see a change."<ref name="wang_03102015" /><ref>{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=Norman Powell talks about decision to stay at UCLA|date=May 22, 2013|work=insidesocal.com|url=http://www.insidesocal.com/ucla/2013/05/22/norman-powell-talks-about-decision-to-stay-at-ucla/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150315012220/http://www.insidesocal.com/ucla/2013/05/22/norman-powell-talks-about-decision-to-stay-at-ucla/|archive-date=March 15, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The Bruins hired [[Steve Alford]] as their new coach.<ref name="yoon_04022013">{{cite news|last=Yoon|first=Peter|title=Norman Powell staying after Howland firing|date=April 2, 2013|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/13723/norman-powell-staying-after-howland-firing|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140426224249/http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/13723/norman-powell-staying-after-howland-firing|archive-date=April 26, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Toronto Raptors (2015–2021)===
====Early years (2015–2017)====

Powell played sparingly for the Raptors over the first half of the [[2016–17 Toronto Raptors season|2016–17 season]]. With [[DeMarre Carroll]] sitting out back-to-back games early on in the season, Powell received a number of starting assignments. He would rise to the occasion every time he got an opportunity, only to go missing in action for a handful of games before his services were needed again.<ref>{{cite web|last=Ganter|first=Mike|url=https://nationalpost.com/sports/basketball/nba/toronto-raptors-cant-find-norman-powell-many-minutes-but-every-time-he-sees-the-court-he-delivers|title=Toronto Raptors can't find Norman Powell many minutes — but every time he sees the court, he delivers|work=NationalPost.com|date=December 12, 2016|access-date=February 7, 2017}}</ref> On December 20, 2016, Powell scored a season-high 21 off the bench in a 116–104 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899862|title=Lowry, Powell lead Raptors to 116-104 win over Nets|work=ESPN.com|date=December 20, 2016|access-date=December 21, 2016}}</ref> He had three more 21-point games over the next three months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/powelno01/gamelog/2017/|title=Norman Powell 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 4, 2017}}</ref> On April 24, 2017, in Game 5 of the Raptors' first-round playoff series against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Powell scored a playoff career-high 25 points to help the Raptors take a 3–2 series lead with a 118–93 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400950415|title=Powell scores 25 as Raptors beat Bucks 118-93 in Game 5|work=ESPN.com|date=April 24, 2017|access-date=April 25, 2017}}</ref>

==== Championship run and breakout seasons (2017–2021) ====
On October 8, 2017, Powell signed a four-year, $42 million contract extension with the Raptors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-extend-norm-powell|title=Raptors Sign Powell To Contract Extension|work=NBA.com|date=October 8, 2017|access-date=October 8, 2017}}</ref><ref name=Wojnarowski>{{cite web|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/20924693/toronto-raptors-norman-powell-agree-four-year-42-million-extension|title=Norman Powell reaches four-year extension with Raptors|work=ESPN.com|date=October 5, 2017|access-date=October 8, 2017}}</ref> The deal, which started with the 2018–19 season, included a player option on the fourth year.<ref name="Wojnarowski" />

his left hand against the Pistons. He returned at the end of February after missing nine games.<ref name=helin_02012020/><ref>{{cite news|last=Grange|first=Michael|title=Norman Powell returns in pre-injury form, but Raptors' comeback flounders|date=February 28, 2020|website=Sportsnet.ca|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/norman-powell-returns-pre-injury-form-raptors-comeback-flounders/|access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref> On March 5, Powell scored a then career-high 37 points in a 121–113 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Kidane|first1=Binyam|last2=Matange|first2=Yash|title=Norman Powell's career-high helps shorthanded Raptors record thrilling win over Warriors in Stephen Curry's return|date=March 6, 2020|website=NBA.com|url=https://in.nba.com/news/norman-powell-career-high-shorthanded-toronto-raptors-golden-state-warriors-steph-currys-return-injury/1xgfveyixy7nj1euub2gkzx2i9|access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref> After averaging a conference-leading 31.3 points on 56 percent shooting and helping the Raptors win three road games that week, he was named the NBA's Eastern Conference player of the week for the first time in his career.<ref>{{cite news|title=Powell named Eastern player of the week|date=March 9, 2020|agency=The Canadian Press|url=https://www.tsn.ca/toronto-raptors-guard-norman-powell-named-eastern-conference-player-of-the-week-1.1455132|access-date=March 10, 2020}}</ref> Toronto advanced in the playoffs to the conference semifinals against the [[Boston Celtics]], which Powell helped tie the series at 3 after scoring 15 of his 23 points in the two overtime periods in a 125–122 win in Game 6.<ref>{{cite news|first=Steven|last=Loung|title='Playoff Powell' helps rescue Raptors' season with clutch Game 6 performance|date=September 10, 2020|website=Sportsnet.ca|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/playoff-powell-helps-rescue-raptors-season-clutch-game-6-performance/|access-date=January 1, 2021}}</ref>

=== Portland Trail Blazers (2021–2022) ===
[[File:Dean Wade vs Norman Powell, Cleveland Cavaliers vs Portland Trail Blazers on November 3, 2021 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Powell with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] guards [[Dean Wade]] of the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] during a 2021 game]]
On March 25, 2021, the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] acquired Powell from Toronto in exchange for [[Gary Trent Jr.]] and [[Rodney Hood]]. At the time, Powell had made 31 starts in his 41 games and was averaging a career-high 19.6 points, while his 3-point field goal percentage of 43.9% ranked 10th in the league.<ref>{{Cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS ACQUIRE NORMAN POWELL FROM TORONTO RAPTORS|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-acquire-norman-powell-toronto-raptors|access-date=2021-03-25|website=NBA.com|language=en}}</ref> On March 27, Powell made his debut and recorded a game-high 22 points in 36 minutes in a 112–105 victory over [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Trail Blazers vs. Magic - Game Recap - March 26, 2021 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401307476|access-date=2021-03-29|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Norman Powell: Newest Portland Trail Blazer delivers efficient performance in debut|url=https://ca.nba.com/news/norman-powell-portland-trail-blazers-guard-shines-in-debut-with-new-team/1d2evle23zo8c11b8pppmrnp5j|access-date=2021-03-29|website=NBA.com Canada {{!}} The official site of the NBA|language=en}}</ref> On August 6, 2021, Powell signed a new, five-year, $90 million contract with the Trail Blazers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Re-Sign Norman Powell|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2021/8/6/trail-blazers-re-sign-norman-powell|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 6, 2021|date=August 6, 2021}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Clippers (2022–2025) ===
On February 4, 2022, Powell was traded, alongside [[Robert Covington]], to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Eric Bledsoe]], [[Justise Winslow]], [[Keon Johnson (basketball, born 2002)|Keon Johnson]], and a 2025 second-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Clippers trade Eric Bledsoe to Trail Blazers for Norman Powell, Robert Covington, per report|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/clippers-trade-eric-bledsoe-to-trail-blazers-for-norman-powell-robert-covington-per-report/|access-date=2022-02-04|website=CBSSports.com|date=February 4, 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Oregonian/OregonLive|first=Aaron Fentress {{!}} The|date=2022-02-04|title=Blazers trade Powell, Covington to Clippers for Bledsoe, Winslow, Johnson: Report|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2022/02/portland-trail-blazers-trade-norman-powell-robert-covington-to-la-clippers-for-eric-bledsoe-justise-winslow-keon-johnson-report.html|access-date=2022-02-04|website=oregonlive|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Clippers will land Norman Powell, Robert Covington in trade with Blazers|url=https://www.nba.com/news/clippers-blazers-trade-norman-powell-eric-bledsoe-robert-covington|access-date=2022-02-04|website=www.nba.com|language=en}}</ref> The trade reunited Powell with former Toronto teammates [[Kawhi Leonard]] and [[Serge Ibaka]],<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-02-07|title=Powell drops 28 in Clips debut, lauds fit with team|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33235618/norman-powell-impresses-28-la-clippers-debut-think-fit-perfectly-here|access-date=2022-02-07|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> the latter of which would be traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on February 10. In his Clippers debut on February 6, Powell scored 28 points and recorded 4 assists in a 137–113 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33235618/norman-powell-impresses-28-la-clippers-debut-think-fit-perfectly-here|title=Norman Powell impresses with 28 in LA Clippers debut: 'Think I can fit perfectly in here'|last=Youngmisuk|first=Ohm|website=ESPN.com|date=February 6, 2022|access-date=February 6, 2022}}</ref> On February 10, he suffered a medial [[sesamoid bone]] fracture in his left foot, which sidelined him for two months.<ref>{{cite web | last=Helin | first=Kurt | title=Clippers' Norman Powell out indefinitely with fracture in left foot | website=NBC Sports | date=2022-02-14 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/clippers-norman-powell-out-indefinitely-with-fracture-in-left-foot | access-date=2025-12-13}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Andrew|last=Greif|title=Norman Powell, Paul George lead Clippers to win over depleted Suns|date=April 6, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/story/2022-04-06/norman-powell-paul-george-lead-clippers-to-win-over-depleted-suns|access-date=April 26, 2022}}</ref> Powell played in a total of seven games for the Clippers after the trade, including two [[NBA play-in tournament|play-in games]], and averaged a career-high 20 points.<ref>{{cite news|first=Andrew|last=Greif|title=Clippers player-by-player report cards for the 2021-22 season|date=April 19, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/story/2022-04-19/clippers-report-cards-2021-22-season|access-date=April 26, 2022}}</ref>

On February 10, 2024, Powell required stitches after he was hit in the face by the elbow of [[Jalen Duren]] during a game against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Turner |first1=Broderick |title=Paul George rallies Clippers past Pistons with 15 fourth-quarter points |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/story/2024-02-10/la-clippers-detroit-pistons-nba-game-recap |website=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 9, 2025 |date=February 10, 2024}}</ref> The incident left him with a scar between his eyes.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Swanson |first1=Mirjam |title=Swanson: Clippers’ Norman Powell understands the grind |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2024/12/18/swanson-clippers-norman-powell-understands-the-grind/ |website=The Orange County Register |access-date=July 9, 2025 |date=December 18, 2024}}</ref>

On February 13, 2025, Powell scored 41 points in a 120–116 overtime win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/clippers-news-norman-powell-reveals-mindset-41-point-outburst-jazz|title=Clippers' Norman Powell reveals mindset that led to 41-point outburst vs. Jazz|website=ClutchPoints|last=Brown|first=Malik|date=February 14, 2025|access-date=February 14, 2025}}</ref> Powell also participated in the 2025 Three-Point Contest, losing in the first round.<ref>{{Cite web |agency=Associated Press |date=2025-02-16 |title=Clippers' Norman Powell falls short in 3-point contest, Mac McClung dunks over car |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2025/02/15/mac-mcclung-pulls-off-1st-nba-dunk-contest-three-peat/ |access-date=2025-02-16 |website=Orange County Register |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Miami Heat (2025–2026) ===

On July 7, 2025, Powell was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in a three-team deal that also included the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-07 |title=Sources: Powell to Heat, Collins to Clips in trade |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45688419/sources-powell-heat-collins-clips-three-team-trade |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-07 |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-norman-powell |title=HEAT ACQUIRE NORMAN POWELL |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> He made his Heat debut on October 22, recording 28 points, nine rebounds and four assists in a 125–121 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner score 24 points each and Orlando beats Miami 125-121 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022500081 |access-date=July 11, 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On November 14, Powell scored a season-high 38 points, alongside five rebounds, in a 140–130 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Towns, Shamet power Knicks to a 140-130 win over Heat in NBA Cup game |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022500039 |access-date=July 11, 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 1, 2026, he recorded 36 points, two rebounds and two assists in a 118–112 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Norman Powell scores 36 points to lead Heat past Pistons 118-112 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022500472 |access-date=July 11, 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On February 1, Powell was named to his first [[2026 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Game]] as a Eastern Conference reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2026 NBA All-Star reserves announced on NBC/Peacock |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2026-all-star-reserves |access-date=2026-02-02 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

The Heat ended the season with a 43–39 record and the tenth place in the Eastern Conference. In their April 14 play-in game against the [[Charlotte Hornets]], Powell recorded eleven points and two rebounds in a 127–126 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LaMelo Ball's layup, Miles Bridges' block at buzzer give Hornets 127-126 win over Heat in play-in |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0052500111 |access-date=July 11, 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

=== Chicago Bulls (2026–present) ===
On July 10, 2026, Powell signed a two-year, $45 million contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Chicago Bulls Sign Norman Powell|date=July 10, 2026|work=Bulls.com|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-sign-norman-powell|access-date=July 10, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Powell has two older sisters, Joniece and Margaret. He majored in history at UCLA.<ref name=ucla_bio/>

In October 2017, Powell teamed with web host [[GoDaddy]] to launch his website and his first [[single (music)|single]], "No Problem".<ref>{{cite news|last=Loung|first=Steven|title=Raptors' Powell launches music website, releases song 'No Problem'|date=October 30, 2017|website=Sportsnet.ca|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/raptors-powell-launches-music-website-releases-song-no-problem/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222105014/http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/raptors-powell-launches-music-website-releases-song-no-problem/|archive-date=December 22, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/GoDaddy-Canada-and-Toronto-Raptor-Norman-Powell-team-up-to-inspire-Canadian-small-businesses-1006175633|title=GoDaddy Canada and Toronto Raptor Norman Powell team up to inspire Canadian small businesses|work=businessinsider.com|date=October 30, 2017|access-date=December 23, 2017}}</ref>
